notes.summary: Conditional reconstruction of bounded411412 scaling, Green, reference and nonordered calculus, including universal coercivity without bounded-MA domination. The geometric and primary-chain audit remains incomplete.
notes.detailedSummary: At the designated quotient and explicit CLD/GR foundation boundary, reconstructs all-stage bounded Green, mixed moments, the42C estimate, actual Gauss reference, fixed fibres and atoms, midpoint I/8, endpoint and uniform third-slot absolute moments, maximum-energy control, and universal full-dual coercivity. These deductions do not certify nonalgebraization, analytic finite-energy representation or existence.
notes.text:
This is a conditional bounded-calculus reconstruction, not a complete audit or a solution of P16.7. The carrier is the designated compact Hausdorff good smooth separated boundaryless pure surface X=(G_m^2)^an_K/<(s^8,2),(3,s^8)>, K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8). Injective torus charts have tau=(-log|z1|,-log|z2|), rho=|tau|^2/2 and theta=DD rho. The quotient's existence and genuine nonalgebraization are not newly certified. Let C be the ENTIRE minimal continuous CLD psh class of finite real weights rho+a, not one approximation stage. MA(a)=theta_a^2, B(a,b)=theta_a theta_b, theta_a=theta+DDa, and E(a)=1/3 integral a[theta^2+B(a,0)+MA(a)]. Raw mass is two.

The exact analytic boundary is CLD v2 (25 July 2025):15.7.1, separated pure-dimensional analytic spaces with analytic boundary carry the calibrated tropical calculus;8.1.7–8 define the entire minimal continuous sheaf;8.2.4 gives continuous convex nondecreasing composition;8.5.1,8.5.5 and8.7.1–4 give positive recursive products, local uniform continuity and symmetry for continuous psh and positive closed currents;8.8.4–5 give dpsh extension and smooth DD-null reference invariance;7.2.8–12 give Radon top currents and coefficient measures on locally differentially separated charts;5.11.1 gives smooth Stokes/Green including boundary, zero here. Smooth approximation/partitions6.2.4–8, explicit torus/annulus Shilov boundaries, the moment-form dimension rule and raw2! convention are named conventional foundations. GR v2 (17 September 2025), unnumbered Section1.2 is the CLD-to-classical bridge; Definition4.1 tests all curves after all complete analytic extensions, Proposition4.2 supplies functoriality and decreasing nets,6.3 describes all affinoid Shilov points by full graded dimension,6.4 is affinoid Shilov maximum, and6.5 requires an already USC POINTWISE limit. Deeper Berkovich/Temkin/Ducros/intersection and Wanner/Thuillier curve inputs remain conventional at their precise scopes. The whole immediate retained applied units were read, but their recursive audit and the historical geometric/generated/descent audit are unfinished. No supplied note or verdict is a premise. All deductions below have this explicit input boundary.

All-stage Green proof. Complete smooth gradients in the positive Hilbert seminorm against positive closed(1,1) T, locally with nonnegative smooth cutoffs. A uniformly zero smooth sequence with strong gradient limit pairs to zero with every smooth Hilbert test beta because integral d'f_j Jbeta T=-integral f_j d'(Jbeta)T->0; coefficient measures are finite, and such tests are dense. Continuous bounded multipliers act with their uniform norm bound. Partitions/Leibniz patch local approximants. If L_Tf=DD(fT) is signed Radon, smooth approximation gives Q_T(f,g)=-integral g L_Tf and Q_(T,chi)(f)=1/2 integral f^2 DDchi T-integral chi f L_Tf. For uniformly convergent psh-domain f_j, nested cutoffs chi,eta with eta=1 near supp chi and |f_j|<=A on the WHOLE supp eta yield, epsilon=||f_j-f_k|| there,
Q_(T,chi)(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon^2||DDchi T||TV/2+2A epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta T||TV.
Positivity bounds the local masses by the eta mass. Strong gradients are therefore Cauchy; smooth diagonal approximants and distributional positivity give a uniformly closed sheaf containing smooth psh. Minimality includes all continuous stages. Differences and finite patching give Q_T(f,g)=-integral f DD(gT)=-integral g DD(fT), Q_T(f)>=0. Smooth one-variable compositions with bounded continuous derivative have the strong chain rule. No indicator gradient rule or8.6.7 arbitrary-multiplier closedness is used.

Cubic expansion gives E'(a_t)=integral(b-a)MA(a_t), E''(a_t)=-2Q_theta_at(b-a). Thus E is concave and monotone, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c, and E(b)-E(a)=1/3 integral(b-a)[MA(a)+B(a,b)+MA(b)]. Exact terms have zero mass by Stokes. Tangent gives D(MA(q))=E(q)-integral q MA(q), where D(mu)=sup_C[E(a)-integral a mu]; constants force mass two when finite. For nonpositive p,q,r of energies>=-C, the three nonnegative terms of -3E(q) imply D(MA(q))<=2C, integral(-p)MA(q)<=3C, integral(-p)B(q,r)<=6C, and Q_theta_q(p),Q_theta(p)<=6C. The mixed bound uses B(q,r)<=2MA((q+r)/2).

For f=a-b, I=integral f(MA(b)-MA(a))=Q_theta_a(f)+Q_theta_b(f), g=(a+b)/2,h=w-g, Green gives Q_theta_w(f)-I/2=Q_theta_a(f,h)-Q_theta_b(f,h). The bound |h|<=-w+(-a-b)/2 gives MA moments6C, mixed moments12C, and Q_theta_a(h),Q_theta_b(h)<=12C+3C+6C=21C. Direct-sum Cauchy–Schwarz proves Q_theta_w(f)<=Psi_C(I)=I/2+sqrt(42CI).

Actual reference and grid proof. Fix one coordinate Gauss point and use the actual other-coordinate curve over its fixed completed residue field. Annulus Shilov comparison with affine harmonic endpoint interpolation makes q^2/2+a(Gauss(q,r2)) convex; period one bounds subgradients between q-1/2 and q+1/2. Both Gauss restrictions are coordinate1/2-Lipschitz. Shrinking rectangular polyannuli gives a(x)<=a(Gauss(tau(x))), hence normalized sup0 implies -1/2<=a|S<=0. Off S a Laurent polynomial has strict cancellation, so on an ordinary neighborhood coordinate tropicalization has dimension<=1 and its top form vanishes. Identity-moment calibration CLD14.5.2–3 and integration5.10.1–2 give the ACTUAL theta^2=2Lebesgue on S and integral(-a)theta^2<=1.

For each finite N-grid, finitely many coordinate paths partition into injective boxes. CLD18.6.2, on separated boundaryless equidimensional source with the smooth coordinate map, identifies DD logmax(1,|z2|/r2) with the actual fixed Gauss-fibre curve current, coefficient one. A collar cap w=max(0,delta+epsilon psi-rho0), extended by zero, has theta_w=epsilon DDpsi on an inner path. Primitive degree-one calibration and radial Cauchy–Schwarz give squared endpoint difference<=length/epsilon times Q_theta_w(f). Positivity gives strong restriction convergence for ambient smooth approximants; uniform convergence gives endpoints at all continuous stages. Summing gives fixed nonpositive tests w_l and A_N with |f(xi)-f(o)|<=A_N max_l sqrt(Q_theta_w_l(f)). Include w0=0 and A1=0.

At full graded-dimension-two x, Abhyankar excludes a Laurent support kernel; smaller-error completion preserves initials. Two independent homogeneous Laurent initials give a weighted Gauss image. CLD11.6.5(c) applies at relative interior, dimensions<=2 and reduced target;11.6.3 gives a compact finite-flat singleton-fibre representative of degree D>0. CLD18.6.2 and calibration14.5.2–3 give raw top log-max mass D at x (equivalently2! times the gradient simplex area1/2 times D). The same bounded collar cap gives an actual w_x in C with MA(w_x)>=alpha_x delta_x, alpha_x>0. This uses the stated conventional graded and finite-flat boundary, not an accepted older note.

For C_C={sup a=0,E(a)>=-C}, define C_N=max(C,max_l[-E(w_l)],0), Omega_C(t)=min(1,inf_N[4/N+4A_N sqrt(Psi_C_N(t))]), H_C(t)=Omega_C(t)+sqrt(6C)(sqrt(t)+sqrt(Psi_C(t))), and T_C(t)=Omega_C(t)+2sqrt(6C)sqrt(Psi_C(t)). These nondecreasing moduli tend to zero: fix N, let t->0, then N->infinity. Twice integrating affine E'' gives exact midpoint deficit I/8. The difference on S is coordinate1-Lipschitz; grid oscillation and both maxima zero give integral|a-b|theta^2<=Omega. Smooth ramps sqrt(f^2+epsilon^2), paired with signed Radon DD(cR), give
integral|f|MA(c)<=Omega+sqrt(Q_theta_c(f)Q_theta_c(c))+sqrt(Q_theta(f)Q_theta(c)).
Uniform ramp convergence requires neither DD of the ramp to be Radon nor indicator gradients. For c=a,b this is <=H_C(I); for ANY c in C_C it is <=T_C(I). For fixed normalized w, D=max(C,-Ew,0), it is <=Omega+[sqrt(Q_theta_w(w))+sqrt(Q_theta(w))]sqrt(Psi_D(I)). Tangent at a,b and finite-max closure give both gains E(max(a,b))-E(a/b) in[0,H_C(I)], hence |Ea-Eb|<=H_C(I). The fixed atom directly gives full-point difference tending to zero, and alpha_x(-a(x))<=D(MA(w_x))+C bounds those values below.

Scaling reconstruction: normalized a, A=integral(-a)theta^2<=1, q0=Q_theta(a),q1=Q_theta_a(a) give C=-Ea=A+2q0/3+q1/3 and -E(ta)=tA+t^2(1-t/3)q0+t^3q1/3<=t+1.5t^2C by integrating E'' and positivity. For any mass-two finite-full-dual mu, B=D(mu), the scaled dual gives integral(-a)mu<=A+B/t+1.5tC. Optimize t in(0,1], treating B=0 by t->0, to get integral(-a)mu<=1+B+sqrt(6BC). Therefore Fmu(a)<=-C+1+B+sqrt(6BC) and Fmu>=-eta implies C<=[sqrt(6B)+sqrt(10B+4+4eta)]^2/4. This is UNIVERSAL coercivity, with no domination hypothesis. The unit-energy criterion follows by tau=[2max(1,sqrt(1.5C))]^-1, for which -E(tau a)<=3/4: N<=D+1 and D<=2N+1.5N^2. Bounded domination mu<=lambda nu, both masses two, similarly yields D(mu)<=lambda(1+B)+1.5lambda^2B. In particular actual point atoms imply D(2delta_x)<infinity, not the Dirac equation.

The full standalone reconstruction is in scoped-paper.tex; its entire proof companion is proof-companion.txt. Original representability, envelopes and prescribed-measure existence are not established by these conditional bounded deductions.

notes.summary: Universal full-dual maximizing nets have common energy, moving moments and genuine weak MA limits, with exact limiting dual energy. Prescribed-measure identification and analytic representation remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: For every positive mass-two finite-full-dual Radon measure, I is bounded by functional deficits and the nonordered maximum estimate makes energies Cauchy without domination. Actual cap separation gives dense continuous tests; Green and Riesz give common weak limits nu and omega. D(nu)=lim D(MA(ai))=e-p and ai converges in L1(nu). Only signed mu integrals are proved convergent.
notes.text:
This uses only earlier own note n1, with its explicit conditional analytic-foundation boundary. Let mu be ANY prescribed positive Radon measure of raw mass two and B=D(mu)<infinity. No support or bounded-MA-domination assumption is imposed. Every normalized full-dual maximizing net a_i has Fmu(a_i)->B and eventually Fmu>=-1; n1 coercivity confines every such tail to the same fixed C_C. If epsilon_a=B-Fmu(a), exact midpoint deficit and the full supremum give
I(a,b)/8=Fmu((a+b)/2)-(Fmu(a)+Fmu(b))/2 <=(epsilon_a+epsilon_b)/2,
so I(a,b)<=4(epsilon_a+epsilon_b). This works on a product of TWO different maximizing nets as well.

Because both finite-max energy gains lie in[0,H_C(I)], their difference proves |Ea-Eb|<=H_C(I), with no factor two. Thus the real energies converge to one finite e universally, without L1(mu) or domination. The fixed-test estimate gives Cauchyness in L1(MA(w)) for each fixed bounded w, and the atom estimate gives finite Cauchy values at every full point. Banach and real completeness give limits; product-index comparison shows independence of the maximizing net. These are not yet analytic representatives.

Here are complete quantitative moving-moment arguments. Put R(a)=integral a theta^2, U(a)=integral a B(a,0), P(a)=integral a MA(a), f=a-b. Then
|R(a)-R(b)|<=Omega_C(I),
|U(a)-U(b)|<=T_C(I),
|P(a)-P(b)|<=H_C(I)+sqrt(12CI).
For P, split into integral f MA(a)+integral b(MA(a)-MA(b)); Green with T=theta_a+theta_b bounds the second by sqrt(Q_T(b)I)<=sqrt(12CI). For U, split into integral f B(a,0)+integral b DD(f theta). Ramp Green with B(a,0)=theta^2+DD(a theta) bounds the first absolute integral by Omega+sqrt(6C)sqrt(Psi_C(I)); Green bounds the second by the same square-root term. Hence all R,U,P have common finite limits. Also |integral a MA(b)-P(b)|<=H_C(I), so ALL FOUR cross moving MA moments of any two maximizing nets converge to the same p=lim P(a_i). Green gives |integral a B(a,b)-P(a)|<=sqrt(6CI), proving the corresponding mixed moving limits as well.

The measure-determining step is actual analytic-space density. The span V of C consists of A(p-q), A>0, p,q in C, by grouping coefficients and filling convex averages with zero. It is a vector lattice because
max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A[max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-(q+s)/2].
It contains constants and separates points. Different tropical classes are separated by a centered quadratic cap supported in a small injective tropical ball. Distinct points in the same tropical fibre have different norms for a Laurent polynomial P; choose c>0 so psi=logmax(1,|P|/c) differs. It is bounded continuous psh on the larger polyannulus, including zeros by smooth convex capped logarithms and regularized maxima. For sufficiently small epsilon, a collar cap max(0,delta+epsilon psi-rho0) belongs to C and at the common central tropical value differs by epsilon times the psi difference. Thus V separates actual Berkovich points.
For h continuous and eta>0, each pair x,y admits v_xy in V agreeing with h at x,y. For fixed x, finitely many neighborhoods where v_xy>h-eta cover X; their maximum v_x is everywhere above h-eta, equals h(x), and is below h+eta near x. A finite cover of these latter neighborhoods and the minimum of the corresponding v_x approximates h uniformly. This proves density using only compact Hausdorff finite covers.

For fixed normalized w and D=max(C,-Ew,0), Green gives
|integral w(MA(a)-MA(b))|<=sqrt(12D I),
|integral w(B(a,0)-B(b,0))|<=sqrt(Q_theta(w)Psi_C(I)).
The first uses transgression and Q_(theta_a+theta_b)(w)<=12D. Each genuine bounded measure is therefore Cauchy against V. Approximate any continuous h uniformly by v in V; common mass two bounds the two error integrals by4||h-v||infinity. The limiting linear functionals on C(X,R) are positive of norm two. The compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation theorem gives actual positive Radon weak limits nu of MA(a_i) and omega of B(a_i,0), both mass two. Product-index comparison proves common limits for all maximizing nets. No sequential weak compactness, metrizability or countable determining set is presumed.

The full dual is continuous along THIS maximizing construction. For fixed i, integral a_i nu=lim_j integral a_i MA(a_j). The preceding moving-moment bounds, uniformly small on product tails, imply integral a_i nu-P(a_i)->0. Therefore integral a_i nu->p. For every fixed w, tangent gives E(w)-integral w MA(a_i)<=Ea_i-P(a_i); passing weakly and taking the supremum gives D(nu)<=e-p. The competitors a_i give the reverse inequality. Hence
D(nu)=e-p=lim_i D(MA(a_i))<=2C,
and the SAME net also maximizes for nu. For each fixed pair i,j, pass the UNIFORM third-slot estimate integral|a_i-a_j|MA(a_k)<=T_C(I(a_i,a_j)) to the weak limit nu against the continuous absolute difference. This proves L1(nu) Cauchyness, hence a finite measurable L1 limit with integral p. Finally integral a_i mu=Ea_i-Fmu(a_i)->r=e-B. This signed-integral limit is not asserted to imply L1(mu).

For each fixed t in[0,1], actual bounded product expansion gives MA(ta_i)->(1-t)^2theta^2+2t(1-t)omega+t^2nu. Scalar cubic coefficients also converge: q0=R-U, q1=U-P and the n1 scaling identity expresses E(ta_i) through R,U,P. These are weak limits of GENUINE bounded analytic MA products, not an alternative inverse operator. No conclusion identifies nu with mu, identifies an L1 class with an analytic weight, or extends the new nonordered estimates to every generated endpoint. Complete arguments appear in scoped-paper.tex, with all input boundaries retained.

notes.summary: One uniform cap family controls all points in local compact finite Gauss-fibre families, giving uniform maximizing-net convergence there. The required Shilov-neighborhood basis remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Fixed Laurent initials and a finite-flat singleton-Gauss representative yield properness concentration. Compact parameter bounds give one collar and epsilon, uniformly bounded cap energies, and atom coefficients at least epsilon squared at every fibre point. Nonordered moments imply uniform convergence. Shrinking radial polyannuli need not fit ordinary target neighborhoods, so this does not resolve upper control or representability.
notes.text:
This uses earlier own notes n1 and n2, at their explicit bounded analytic-foundation boundary. It proves a LOCAL UNIFORM FINITE-GAUSS-FIBRE sector of the proposed geometric route; it does not construct the required Shilov-neighborhood basis or solve analytic representability.

Fix a full graded-dimension-two point x. Use the SAME two fixed Laurent polynomials P1,P2 and compact finite-flat representative f:V->U from n1, with positive degree D and singleton Gauss fibre {x} at g0=f(x). V,U are analytic neighborhoods, so x and g0 lie in their ordinary interiors. Choose a small compact rectangle J of log radii around g0 whose continuous weighted Gauss section sigma(J) lies in Int U. The section is only a continuous topological map, not asserted analytic. Properness gives a stronger concentration assertion: for any ordinary neighborhood O of x, V\O is compact and f(V\O) is compact and avoids g0 by the singleton fibre. A target neighborhood of g0 avoids that image. Shrinking J makes every point of Theta=f^-1(sigma(J)) cap V lie in O. In particular choose O inside Int V and inside a small inner base-coordinate tropical ball. Theta is compact, and every point in its finite fibres has full graded dimension two because its complete residue field is finite over the two-dimensional weighted Gauss field.

Uniform cap construction. On a larger injective base tropical ball of radius R, put rho0=|tau-tau(x)|^2/2 and psi_r=logmax(1,|P1|/r1,|P2|/r2). Laurent polynomials are bounded on the compact larger polyannulus and r_i have positive minima on J. Thus 0<=psi_r<=M0 uniformly. Choose one delta>0 below R^2/4 and one epsilon>0 with delta+epsilon M0 less than the minimum of rho0 on a fixed outer collar. Every w_r=max(0,delta+epsilon psi_r-rho0), extended by zero, is an actual global continuous member of C; n1's capped logarithm and maximum construction also verifies the polynomial-zero points. Uniformly 0<=w_r<=M=delta+epsilon M0. Shrink J by properness so Theta lies where rho0<delta/2. On this inner region theta_w_r=epsilon DDpsi_r.

At EVERY point y of each finite Gauss fibre, CLD18.6.2 and finite-flat calibration14.5.2–3 give the local log-max top mass d_y delta_y, where d_y is the positive integer local degree and sum_y d_y=D. This is the actual fibre current on ordinary boundaryless interiors, at the same raw convention as n1's atom. Therefore MA(w_r)>=epsilon^2 d_y delta_y>=epsilon^2 delta_y. This coefficient is uniform in r,y; no extra varying-ground-field factor is inserted. Normalize w_hat_r=w_r-sup w_r. Since -M<=w_hat_r<=0, energy monotonicity gives E(w_hat_r)>=-2M uniformly.

For any a,b in C_C set D0=max(C,2M,0). The fixed-test absolute estimate and the6D0 gradient bounds in n1 give, uniformly in r,
integral|a-b|MA(w_r)<=Omega_C(I)+2sqrt(6D0)sqrt(Psi_D0(I)).
Divide by epsilon^2 at each fibre atom to bound |a(y)-b(y)| uniformly over Theta. For full-dual maximizing tails, n2 gives I<=4(epsilon_a+epsilon_b)->0. Thus their restrictions are uniformly Cauchy on compact Theta. Completeness of C(Theta,R) gives a finite continuous uniform limit equal to the full-point tuple. No metrizability is needed. Its continuity, together with the proved concentration of nearby finite Gauss fibres at x, controls its values along this family near x.

The remaining step is not supplied. An ordinary target neighborhood of a Gauss point can exclude cancellation points with the SAME coordinate radii. Therefore shrinking coordinate polyannuli need not lie in U. Pulling them back through this LOCAL finite-flat representative does not construct the affinoid neighborhoods needed for the all-Shilov formula. Properness and this uniform cap family alone do not prove that all required Shilov boundaries belong to Theta. Consequently this result does not imply equality between the full-point tuple and its USC upper relaxation, positivity, generated membership, or the prescribed equation. The entire proof and this limitation are in scoped-paper.tex, Proposition uniformfibres; all primary foundations remain as in n1.

notes.summary: Constructs a canonical actual USC upper relaxation from all affinoid Shilov limits and proves the exact nonnegative defect K=D(mu)-D(nu). Positivity and original existence remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: The upper relaxed tail limit is normalized, common to maximizing nets and determined by all finite affinoid Shilov boundaries. It agrees with the uniform Gauss limit but may exceed the full-point tuple. One-sided variations give K>=0 and integral w(nu-mu)<=K. A precise, unproved two-sided perturbation condition would force nu=mu; neither this condition nor finite-energy analytic membership is established.
notes.text:
This uses earlier own notes n1 and n2; the local uniform sector n3 is relevant only to the stated unresolved geometric step. The conclusions are a canonical actual USC UPPER RELAXATION and an exact dual defect, not an analytic finite-energy solution.

Let a_i be a normalized net maximizing the full bounded dual for positive mass-two finite-dual mu. With n2 limits e=lim Ea_i, p=lim integral a_i MA(a_i), r=lim integral a_i mu=e-B, and nu=weak-lim MA(a_i), define
K=p-r=B-D(nu)=lim_i integral a_i(MA(a_i)-mu).
All equalities follow from n2's exact D(nu)=e-p. The sign and the entire allowable first-variation conclusion can be proved explicitly. Write k_i=integral a_i(MA(a_i)-mu). For0<t<=1, the second derivative of Fmu((1-t)a_i) has absolute value<=12C, because Q_theta_s a_i(a_i)<=6C. Integral Taylor remainder gives Fmu((1-t)a_i)>=Fmu(a_i)-t k_i-6Ct^2. Its value is at most B, so k_i>=-epsilon_i/t-6Ct. First take the net limit, then t->0, proving K>=0.
For fixed normalized w, D=max(C,-Ew,0), the Hilbert inequality Q_T(w-a_i)<=2Q_T(w)+2Q_T(a_i) and n1's moment bounds give a second derivative bound48D along (1-t)a_i+tw. Therefore
integral w(MA(a_i)-mu)-k_i<=epsilon_i/t+24Dt.
Taking the two limits gives integral w(nu-mu)<=K for EVERY w in C. Constants remove the normalization. These one-sided inequalities on a convex positivity class do not imply nu=mu: C is not closed under negation or arbitrary positive scaling, although its linear span is dense.

For clarity, a sufficient replacement variation condition has a complete implication proof. Suppose a uniformly dense real test space W admits for every h some t_h>0,L_h<infinity such that late actual weights a_i+th belong to C for |t|<=t_h and
|Fmu(a_i+th)-Fmu(a_i)-t integral h(MA(a_i)-mu)|<=L_h t^2.
Both signs and maximality imply |integral h(MA(a_i)-mu)|<=epsilon_i/t+L_h t. Passing first to the weak net limit and then t->0 yields integral h(nu-mu)=0. Density and finite masses give nu=mu. The needed actual perturbations are NOT proved; theta degenerates off its coordinate skeleton. This implication also supplies no analytic representative by itself.

Canonical actual USC reconstruction. Let ell(x)=lim_i a_i(x) at every full point, supplied by n2. For each tail i set b_i(y)=sup_{j>=i}a_j(y), and R_i(x)=inf_{ordinary O containing x} sup_{y in O}b_i(y). If R_i(x)<c for a finite c, one such O gives the same strict upper bound at all its points, so R_i is USC, including -infinity. The R_i decrease, hence R=inf_i R_i is USC with R<=0. This is a topological construction; none of b_i,R_i,R is thereby psh or generated. Adding a continuous local rho commutes with upper relaxation and its decreasing infimum.

There is a precise all-Shilov formula, independent of the maximizing net:
rho(x)+R(x)=inf_{affinoid neighborhoods A of x in the chart} max_{xi in Gamma_A}(rho(xi)+ell(xi)).
Proof: every such pure surface affinoid has a FINITE Shilov boundary of full graded dimension two by GR6.3. Each q_j=rho+a_j is classically psh, so GR6.4 bounds q_j on A by max_Gamma_A q_j. This finite maximum converges to max_Gamma_A(rho+ell), and x is in the ordinary interior of A. Hence the upper relaxed limit is at most that maximum and then its infimum. Conversely for any ordinary neighborhood O and any tail i, choose an affinoid neighborhood A contained in O, using goodness and boundarylessness. Its finite Shilov points lie in O; their tail suprema are at least their finite limits. Thus sup_{y in O,j>=i}q_j(y)>=max_Gamma_A(rho+ell)>=the stated affinoid infimum. Infimize over O and i to prove the reverse inequality. The formula glues across continuous affine reference changes. Since ell is common to all maximizing nets, so is R.

Pointwise tail suprema give ell(x)<=R(x) at full points. On the real Gauss torus the restrictions g_i are equi-Lipschitz and pointwise Cauchy, hence uniformly Cauchy by a finite grid argument. Their continuous uniform limit g has maximum zero. Since a_i(y)<=g_i(tau(y)), upper relaxation gives R(y)<=g(tau(y)). At Gauss points R>=ell=g, so R|S=g and max_XR=0. In particular R is an actual nontrivial USC function, with possible poles.

This does NOT establish agreement R=ell at every full point, classical psh positivity, membership in an adequate actual finite-energy domain, energy E(R)=e, identification nu=MA(R), or nu=mu. GR6.5 assumes full POINTWISE convergence to an already USC function; the present full-point tuple plus upper relaxation does not meet that hypothesis. Decreasing-net closure cannot be applied to unproved positive tail suprema or their regularizations. Note n3 supplies uniform convergence only on the specified compact finite-Gauss-fibre family, not the missing Shilov-neighborhood basis. The original arbitrary-support existence and representability gates remain intact. Entire proofs appear in scoped-paper.tex and the separate whole proof-companion.txt.
